body:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool us-west2-spot is experiencing sustained preemptions. Autoscaler failed to reclaim capacity -> queue length spike. Affected routes: /v1/generate (high), /v1/chat (medium). Current queue: ~4.2k requests, p95 latency > 3.8s, p99 > 12s. Link: https://console.re/r/incident/1765432100 :rotating_light:

emma (SRE): ACK. I'm pulling the autoscaler logs now. Did we hit any new quota limits or is this pure spot churn?

raj (Infra): looks like a large spot eviction wave across the pool. Autoscaler attempted scale-up but kept getting preempted nodes immediately. There's a race where new spot VMs are evicted before kube join completes. Not seeing quota errors in GCP.

maria (ProdEng): Customer impact? Any severe throttling or 429s? We should get CS ready to notify top customers.

noah (CustomerSuccess): I'm getting reports from 3 customers (enterprise tier) about timeouts. Will hold until we know scope. Please send quick PSR when we have numbers.

emma (SRE): quick mitigation plan: 1) route critical traffic to dedicated pool (redwood-dedicated-usw2) 2) temporarily raise min nodes on fallback-on-demand pool 3) prevent autoscaler from relying solely on spot for critical routes.

raj (Infra): I can bump the on-demand fallback pool. Increasing nodeGroup min from 0 -> 4 for immediate capacity. Patching now:

ops-bot: ran command: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize redwood-fallback-usw2 --size 4 --zone=us-west2-b` -> started

emma (SRE): good. While that comes up, we should disable spot-provisioning for the critical service routing policy so new requests don't land on spot-pinned node selectors. Patch in the router config: 

```
# router config patch
- match: route == "/v1/generate"
  prefer_pool: redwood-dedicated-usw2
  fallback: redwood-on-demand-usw2
```

emma (SRE): applying now.

ops-bot: router patch applied. Traffic re-route started (approx 30s propagation).

maria (ProdEng): Can we quantify how many tokens/requests are currently on spot vs dedicated? Need numbers for incident note.

emma (SRE): pulling metrics...

emma (SRE): snapshot: total inflight requests 4.3k. Estimated impacted (queued on spot) ~2.6k. Estimated error rate bump: from 0.2% -> 3.7% on /v1/generate. No 5xx storm yet but tail latency is bad.

noah (CustomerSuccess): forwarding to affected customers that we're failing over to dedicated for stability. They'll want ETA for full recovery.

raj (Infra): fallback nodes are joining. I see 4 new on-demand nodes Ready. Autoscaler still flagged some spot groups as unhealthy, I'm marking those pools to drain to avoid churn. Running: `kubectl cordon -l pool=spot-usw2 && kubectl drain ...`

emma (SRE): after drain completes, schedule a controlled scale-up of dedicated capacity to absorb load and then roll back router preferences once spot stability confirmed. Also open a quota/support request with cloud to investigate the eviction wave source (maintenance or capacity reclaim).

ops-bot: drain in progress, cordoned 18 nodes. Pod disruption budget checks passing.

maria (ProdEng): Customer-facing message draft: "We're experiencing degraded performance due to preemptible GPU interruptions in us-west2. We've activated dedicated fallback capacity and are stabilizing traffic. Some customers saw higher latencies/timeouts between 14:02-14:12 UTC. Full recovery expected in ~15-30m. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Approve? :thinking_face:

noah (CustomerSuccess): approve. Send now to the three affected customers and post a short note on status.redwood.ai.

emma (SRE): agree. Sending PSR update. Also creating incident issue with immediate follow-ups: 1) autoscaler robustness for high-eviction rate 2) routing policy preferences for critical routes 3) runbook clarification: minimum dedicated fallback for production.

raj (Infra): follow-up: we should add a short cooldown window for spot instance group joins to avoid immediate re-add after eviction; autoscaler is being noisy. I'll prototype a safeguard.

emma (SRE): good. After traffic fully shifted and p95 < 500ms for critical routes, we'll close the on-call bridge. Current p95 for /v1/generate is down to ~480ms after reroute.

ops-bot: monitoring alert cleared for queue spike. p99 still slightly elevated but trending down.

maria (ProdEng): thanks team. Action items assigned in the incident ticket: Raj -> autoscaler guard, Emma -> runbook & postmortem template, Ops -> verify PDBs and drain automation. Noah -> customer follow-ups. We'll do RCA tomorrow with logs and cloud provider feedback.

emma (SRE): closing bridge in 10m unless new regressions. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
